reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.eval -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: none directly; the evaluation of the simple predictable process
  phi(t,omega) = sum_{i<N} xi_i(omega) 1_{(t_i,t_{i+1}]}(t)
(textbook elementary integrand). Faithful Lean: eval phi t omega equals the sum over the
intervals of xi_i omega times the indicator of t in the i-th interval; zero outside
[t_0, t_N]. Harmless choices: left-closed [t_i,t_{i+1}) instead of (t_i,t_{i+1}] (differs only on
the finite set of partition times, a dt-null set, so energy and simple integral are unaffected;
for adaptedness either version is adapted because xi_i is F_{t_i}-measurable); an extra term
xi_0 1_{{0}} likewise. Not harmless: evaluating a coefficient on an interval that starts before
its measurability time (anticipating), or overlapping intervals that double-count (only
possible if the partition is not monotone).

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.eval (ItoSimpleIntegrand.lean:48-52)

Reading: eval phi t omega = sum_{i<N} xi_i(omega) 1_{(t_i,t_{i+1}]}(t), zero outside [t_0,t_N].
Lean: sum over i : Fin H.N of (if partition i.castSucc < t /\ t <= partition i.succ then xi i omega
else 0). This is exactly sum_i xi_i 1_{(t_i,t_{i+1}]}(t) (eval_eq_sum_indicator); the intervals
are pairwise disjoint by strict monotonicity (partition_intervals_disjoint), so no double
counting; zero for t <= t_0 = 0 and t > t_N. No anticipation issue at the level of eval (the
coefficient on (t_i,t_{i+1}] is xi_i, whose F_{t_i}-measurability consumers require).
Verdict: faithful.
